chunks: O creatures of Allāh! Fear Allāh
and anticipate your death by good actions. Purchase everlasting joy by paying transitory things
Get ready for the journey, for you are being driven, and prepare yourself for death, since it is hovering over you.
Be a people who wake up when called,
and who know that this world is not their abode, and so have it changed (with the next).
ai.seo_question: How should one prepare for death according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) employs the metaphor of trade to urge believers to exchange the fleeting, decaying world for the eternal hereafter, a concept deeply rooted in Shia eschatological reflection on *al-fana* (transience). This passage, often cited in sermons regarding the impermanence of worldly power, serves as a spiritual call to awaken from heedlessness (*ghaflah*) and prioritize deeds that yield lasting spiritual capital. It reflects the Shia emphasis on active preparation for death not as a passive end, but as a conscious transition to the abode of truth.

en.sayed-ali-raza: O creatures of Allāh! Fear Allāh
and anticipate your death by good actions. Purchase everlasting joy by paying transitory things — pleasures of this world.
Get ready for the journey, for you are being driven, and prepare yourself for death, since it is hovering over you.
Be a people who wake up when called,
and who know that this world is not their abode, and so have it changed (with the next).
